question.text:
Two hosts, $A$ and $B$, are connected via a single packet switch. The links from $A$ to the switch and from the switch to $B$ both have a data rate of $2 \times 10^7$ bits per second. Each link has a propagation delay of $10$ microseconds.

The switch uses store-and-forward switching and adds a $50$ microsecond processing delay. This delay begins after the entire packet has been received.

If $20,000$ bits of data are to be transmitted from $A$ to $B$ using a packet size of $4,000$ bits, the time elapsed between the transmission of the first bit of data and the reception of the last bit of the data (in microseconds) is $\_\_\_\_$ .
question.subject: Computer Networks

question.text:
Consider the entries shown below in the forwarding table of an IP router.  

The router uses the longest prefix match rule.  

The notation “/N” in a prefix indicates a subnet mask with the most significant N bits set to $1$.

\[
\begin{array}{ll}
\text{Prefix} & \text{Next hop router} \\
192.168.10.0/23 & R1 \\
192.168.10.0/24 & R2 \\
192.168.11.0/24 & R3 \\
192.168.10.128/25 & R4 \\
\end{array}
\]

This router forwards $50$ packets each to $5$ hosts.  

The IP addresses of the hosts are $$192.168.10.15, 192.168.10.130, 192.168.11.25, 192.168.11.140, 192.168.10.200$$

The total number of packets forwarded via the next hop router $R4$ is $\_\_\_\_$.

question.text:
A router has the following entries in its routing table:

\[
\begin{array}{lll}
\text{Destination} & \text{Subnet Mask} & \text{Interface} \\
172.16.0.0 & 255.255.0.0 & \text{IF-0} \\
172.16.128.0 & 255.255.192.0 & \text{IF-1} \\
10.5.5.10 & 255.255.255.255 & \text{IF-2} \\
\text{Default} &  & \text{IF-3} \\
\end{array}
\]

On which interface will the router forward packets addressed to destinations $172.16.150.25$ and $172.16.10.10$ respectively?

  1. IF-$0$ and IF-$1$
     
  2. IF-$1$ and IF-$0$
     
  3. IF-$1$ and IF-$3$
     
  4. IF-$2$ and IF-$0$

question.text:
A bit-stuffing-based framing protocol uses an $8$-bit flag pattern of $01111110$. If the output bitstring after stuffing is $011111011111001$, then the original input bitstring is:

  1. $011111011111001$
     
  2. $0111111111101$
     
  3. $01111111111001$
     
  4. $01111101111101$
